cards.name: Run speed, friction and acceleration
cards.summary: The player runs at 250 units per second. Ground friction drains speed in proportion to the larger of current speed and a 100 unit stop floor. Ground acceleration is 12 and air acceleration is 4.
cards.behavior: Every movement step applies friction first and acceleration second. The step time is the time since the last command, clamped between 1 and 200 milliseconds. Friction acts only on a walkable, non-slick floor and not during knockback. The speed drop equals the larger of speed and the stop floor, times the friction value, times the step seconds. Holding the use key multiplies friction by 3 for a careful stop. Horizontal speed under 1 unit per second snaps to zero. Input is scaled so the strongest axis maps to the full run speed, with 127 as the full analog value. Acceleration adds only the shortfall between speed along the wish direction and the wish speed. On slick floor, during knockback and in the air the air value of 4 applies. In the air, steering against the current velocity multiplies the wish speed by 1.35 so the player can brake. Crouching caps the wish speed at half of the run speed. The friction value of 6 is stored on the player state at spawn. The matching constant in the movement file is not read by the friction code.

constants.unit: per second, multiplied by step seconds

cards.name: Run speed while swinging the saber
cards.summary: Holding attack with the saber slows the run in the medium and strong stances. Fast stance keeps full speed. Backing up during a swing and spinning moves slow the player more.
cards.behavior: Each frame the run speed starts at the base value of 250. If the saber is held and the attack button is down, the speed is multiplied by a stance factor. Fast stance has no factor. Medium stance uses 0.85. Strong stance uses 0.70. If the player is mid-swing and moving backward, the factors are stronger: fast 0.75, medium 0.60, strong 0.45. Spinning saber animations on the legs halve the speed. A cheat variable scales all of these but defaults to 1. The result goes through the normal acceleration code, so the slowdown arrives as a lower speed cap and not as extra friction. This makes fast stance the only stance that can chase while swinging, and it makes strong swings commit the player to the spot.

cards.name: Jump and hold-to-extend force jump
cards.summary: A plain jump launches at 225 units per second under 800 gravity. With force levitation the player keeps holding jump and the climb continues up to 96, 192 or 384 units by level, spending force as it goes.
cards.behavior: Pressing jump sets vertical velocity to 225. While jump stays held and the player is rising, the force jump code takes over. It measures the height above takeoff. While the height is under the plain jump height of 32, or while force remains and jump is still held, and the height is below the level maximum, the vertical velocity is rewritten each step. The new value is the remaining fraction of the maximum height times the level strength, divided by 10, plus 225. So the climb eases off as it nears the ceiling. Between the plain height and the level maximum minus 32 the velocity is capped at 225. Past that the velocity is set to zero. Releasing jump or running out of force ends the boost. While the boost runs, 5 force points drain every 100 milliseconds. The heights are measured from takeoff and the player also has an 18 unit step height on top. Gravity is 800 units per second squared. The player hull spans from 24 below to 40 above its origin, so it is 64 units tall, and these two values are offsets from the origin and not half extents. The default force jump level for a new player is 2 and level scripts raise it to 3.

cards.name: Fall damage thresholds and the crouch roll
cards.summary: Landing speed divided by 10 gives an impact value. Under 50 is free. From 50 the player takes a quarter of the value in damage that ignores armor. A crouch roll after half a second airborne halves the value.
cards.behavior: On landing the impact value is the absolute vertical speed divided by 10. Water cuts it to half in shallow water and to a quarter at chest depth, and full submersion removes it. If the player jumped, the value is instead the drop below the takeoff height minus an allowance, halved. The allowance is the force jump height of the level, but never less than 128. Landing back at or above takeoff height gives no damage. If the player is crouched and has been in the air over 500 milliseconds, a roll runs and halves the value. Values at 75 and above play the far fall event and apply damage. Values from 50 to 74 play the medium fall event and apply damage. Smaller values only play a landing animation. For the player, the damage is the impact value halved twice, so a fall at 1000 units per second gives an impact of 100 and 25 health lost. Fall damage skips armor. Saber-wielding NPCs take none.

cards.name: Force pool, regeneration and power costs
cards.summary: The pool holds 100 points and refills at 1 point per 100 milliseconds while no power is active. Speed costs 50, push and pull 15, mind trick and saber throw 20, jump 10. Grip and lightning cost 1 per tick.
cards.behavior: Force is a single pool for all powers. Regeneration is paused while any force power runs. It is also paused while the saber is thrown. Otherwise one point returns every 100 milliseconds. A power is usable only if the player knows it, its level is above zero, it is not already running and the pool holds at least its cost. Costs come from one table. Jump, speed, push, pull, mind trick and saber throw are paid once at start. Grip and lightning pay a small amount each update while held, and each also needs a higher pool at the start. Heal pays 4 points for every health point restored. Levitation is always available in terms of cost and drains only while the hold-jump boost runs. NPCs pay nothing. The player starts with the full pool and powers at levels set by the first levels of the game, which scripts raise over time. The engine tracks levels from 0 to 3 for each power.

cards.name: Force push and pull
cards.summary: Push and pull reach 384, 448 or 512 units by level. At level 1 the target must be dead ahead. Higher levels use a widening cone and hit several targets, with a cost that rises with the count.
cards.behavior: Both powers search a box around the user with half size equal to the level radius. At cone value 1.0 the user must be aiming straight at the target using a sight trace. Lower values accept anything inside a cone, where the number is the minimum dot product with the view direction. Push cone is 1.0 at level 1, 0.8 at level 2 and 0.6 at level 3. Pull cone is 1.0 for levels 1 and 2 and 0.8 at level 3. Push locks the weapon for 650 milliseconds and pull for 200. After the push the user cannot push again for the length of the animation plus 500 milliseconds. Loose items and rolling thermals are tossed with a knockback value up to 200. Force-usable doors and switches are triggered. A power that finds no target costs only 5 points. At level 3 push and pull cost 15 per target, capped at 50. At level 2 push costs the same count divided by 1.5, also capped at 50. Level 1 always costs 15. NPCs may push again after 200 milliseconds.

cards.name: Force speed as world slow motion
cards.summary: Force speed slows the whole world clock to 0.75, 0.5 or 0.25 for 7.5, 5 or 2.5 seconds of world time. The player keeps normal speed and the camera pulls back by 30, 45 or 60 units.
cards.behavior: Starting speed costs 50 points. The duration is 10000 milliseconds times the level factor, so level 1 lasts 7500, level 2 lasts 5000 and level 3 lasts 2500 milliseconds. While active, the game time scale is set to the level factor. If the time scale is still higher than the target, it falls by 0.05 each update until it reaches the target. The player fires weapons at the normal rate because the fire delay is multiplied by the time scale. The swing damage code multiplies saber damage by one minus the time scale, but strong-stance swings for the player count as level 3. The third-person camera moves back along the view axis by the range mod. It eases in over the first 1000 milliseconds and eases out over the last 500 milliseconds.
capabilities: global slow motion with a player exemption

cards.name: Force grip hold, lift and carry
cards.summary: Grip needs 26 force to start and reaches 512 units. Level 1 only holds the target on the ground. Level 2 lifts and does 6 damage per tick. Level 3 carries the target 128 to 256 units in front of the hand for 9 damage per tick.
cards.behavior: The player must hold the grip input. Starting needs more than 25 force and locks the weapon for 1000 milliseconds. A sight trace out to 512 units picks the target. Level 1 freezes the target in place and ends if the target leaves the ground, and it deals no damage and drains no force. Level 2 lifts the target and ends if the target is not within a forward cone of 0.3 or is farther than 512. Level 3 pulls the target to a point on the view line, with the distance clamped between 128 and 256 units. Damage ticks at random intervals. Against NPCs the interval is 250 to 1000 milliseconds at level 2 and 150 to 750 at level 3. If the player is the target it is 100 to 600 milliseconds. Each damage tick drains 3 force from the user. Grip damage skips armor. A Jedi target can break free with a push at a chance that falls as its evasion skill and the difficulty rise. Dead targets and empty force end the hold.

cards.name: Force lightning beam and arc
cards.summary: Lightning needs 25 force to start and costs 1 per tick. Levels 1 and 2 shoot a 2048 unit line for 1 to 3 damage. Level 3 arcs to every enemy within 512 units in a front cone and does 1 to 5 damage by distance and aim.
cards.behavior: Pressing the lightning input starts the power if the pool is 25 or more and the cooldown has passed. Level 1 is a short burst for the length of its animation. Levels 2 and 3 keep going while the button is held and refresh the end time to 500 milliseconds ahead on each update. While active, the shoot function runs each update and the power drains 1 force each time. Below level 3 a line trace of 2048 units finds the target and the damage is a random 1 to 3. The trace repeats up to 10 times when a Jedi dodges. At level 3 every damageable target in a box of half size 512 that is in view and has a clear line gets hit. The target must satisfy a dot product of at least 0.5 with the view direction. The damage is 1, plus 2 within 100 units or plus 1 within 200, plus 2 above a dot of 0.9 or plus 1 above 0.7. That gives 1 to 5. Saber users take nothing half of the time and 1 otherwise. Targets show a shock effect for 500 milliseconds, or 4000 for droids, dead bodies and walkers. Mind trick on the same table lasts 5, 10 or 15 seconds by level.

cards.name: Force heal
cards.summary: Heal restores up to 25 health in steps of 1, one step per 200 milliseconds, or per 50 at level 3. Each step costs 4 force. Lower levels cancel on attack, damage or movement.
cards.behavior: Heal costs nothing to start and then pays 4 force for each health point. It stops when 25 points were restored, when health is full, or when the pool cannot pay 4. Below level 3 it also stops if the player fires, takes a hit or has a weapon delay running. Below level 2 it also stops if the player moves or jumps. Level 3 can be held while fighting and heals one point every 50 milliseconds. Levels 1 and 2 heal one point every 200 milliseconds. This makes level 3 heal fast enough to offset light fire, while lower levels are only for pauses.

cards.name: Saber stances and swing damage
cards.summary: Fast, medium and strong stances are power levels 1, 2 and 3. Damage per blade sample is 2.5 times the level of the swing animation. Fast transitions play 1.5 times faster and strong ones 0.75 times.
cards.behavior: The damage level comes from the animation that is playing, and not from the offense skill. Fast swings are level 1, medium level 2 and strong level 3. During a real swing each sampled blade hit uses 2.5 times the level, so 2.5, 5 and 7.5. Strong-level animations also do full damage in transitions. Other transitions, parries and idle blade moves use a token 0.1. A held-ready saber does no damage. During a lock or a block, damage is zero. Total damage per victim is summed over the swing and then clamped. For non-saber targets the clamp is 25 to 100. For saber users the clamp is 5 to 100, and the player never takes more than 50 from one hit. Saber users also get a cap tied to hit location. Stance animation timing differs. Fast transitions run 1.5 times faster and strong transitions run 0.75 times as fast. The saber table of speed mods by offense level is not read by the live code. The default stance for the player is medium. The blade is 40 units long, 32 for Reborn and 48 for the dark boss. The blade is sampled along its length in 8 unit steps.

cards.name: Dismemberment chance by body part
cards.summary: A saber hit can remove a limb. The chance for each part comes from per-actor values. The player has 5 for arms and 20 for hands. Enemies default to 100 and lose limbs on every eligible hit.
cards.behavior: A global level selects which parts may come off, from none up to everything, and it defaults to 3 which covers arms, hands, legs, waist and head as far as the level allows. After that, the part gets a roll. The roll is a random whole number from 1 to 100, times a probability scale of 1. The limb comes off only if the roll is at most twice the part value. A value of 100 means certain. A value of 5 gives a 10 percent chance. A value of 20 gives 40 percent. Head, waist and legs are 0 on the player, so they never come off. A dismembered actor cannot lose another part until it is reset. Realistic combat mode skips the roll.
capabilities: one limb loss at a time

cards.name: Saber deflection of blaster bolts
cards.summary: With the saber out, bolts that arrive from the front are blocked. Defense level 1 deflects half of them, levels 2 and 3 deflect about 87 percent. Level 3 always sends them back at an enemy, and higher difficulty lets some weapons through.
cards.behavior: Each frame the saber holder scans a 256 unit box for incoming bolts and thrown sabers heading toward them. It only reacts if the bolt is in front, using a dot product of at least 0.2 with the view. A hit on the blade then rolls. Level 1 deflects when a 0 or 1 roll gives 1, so 50 percent. Level 2 or 3 also deflects when a roll of 0 to 3 is nonzero, so the combined chance is 1 minus the product of 25 percent and 50 percent, which is 87.5 percent. The code comment says 75 percent for level 2 and the real formula gives more. Explosive bolts with splash cannot be deflected. On easy all bolts can be deflected. On medium flechettes and the DEMP2 pass through. On hard the bowcaster and repeater pass through as well. A deflected bolt keeps its speed and changes owner to the deflector. Rockets stop homing. Level 3 aims it at the current enemy 75 percent of the time and otherwise at another enemy in a 0.3 cone, with a small jitter. Level 2 does this with a 25 percent chance. Otherwise the bolt flies toward its shooter with random scatter of up to 0.4 per axis at level 1 and 0.2 at level 2. Swinging, transitions and a thrown saber add more scatter. The player blocks bolts only if automatic blocking is on and the attack button is not held.

cards.name: Parry cooldown by defense level
cards.summary: After a block the player cannot start another for 300, 150 or 50 milliseconds at defense levels 1, 2 and 3. A parry cancels the attacker damage and turns the victim toward the attacker.
cards.behavior: A block picks one of five directions from where the hit landed relative to the eye. The upper band, the mid band and the low band use different dot thresholds. A parry is played only if the defender is not attacking, in a transition, in a bounce or in a knockaway. A parry removes the damage that the attacker had queued for the defender in this frame. The defender then takes the attacker as an enemy if it is on another team. After the block, a cooldown from a small table stops another block. Level 0 has an effectively infinite cooldown. The player uses the table. NPCs use a time computed from difficulty.

cards.name: Thrown saber range, cost and homing
cards.summary: Throwing costs 20 force to be usable. Range is 256 at level 1 and 400 at levels 2 and 3. Level 3 homes on an enemy and costs 1 force per 100 milliseconds. The blade spins at 600, 800 or 1200 degrees per second.
cards.behavior: The alt-fire input throws the saber if it is lit, not in water and not blocked by a wall. It must have at least 20 force. At level 3 the start also pays 10, then 1 per 100 milliseconds while the input stays held. When the pool is empty the saber returns. The blade flies at 500 units per second under control for levels 2 and 3. At level 3 it picks an enemy and homes in on it. Level 1 flies straight and returns when it reaches its range. Levels 1 and 2 return after 3000 milliseconds or when the input is released after at least 1000 milliseconds out. The return distance shrinks by 25 per update. A dropped saber on the floor can be pulled back by pressing attack. If it is lost for 15 seconds the player gets it back, or 5 seconds for NPCs. A flying saber is lethal. Its damage per sample is 10 for the player, 2.5 for NPCs and 0.1 on the way back.
capabilities: throw and recall of the saber
enemy-seeking flight at the top level

cards.name: Saber lock struggle
cards.summary: Two blades lock when two opposing fighters on the ground are 8 to 80 units apart, within 18 units in height. The lock lasts up to 10 seconds. Each attack-button tap advances the struggle by offense level plus a random bonus.
cards.behavior: A lock starts when a swing meets an opposing swing, both fighters stand on the floor, neither was hurt in the last second and each is inside the other 40 degree horizontal and 180 degree vertical view. The squared distance must be from 64 to 6400. Once locked, both are fixed for the lock time. Each tap on attack, not a hold, moves the animation by a strength value. Strength is the offense level plus a random number from 0 to the difficulty value. The two bosses use 5 plus the same random number. The first side whose animation reaches its end wins. If the time runs out the lock ends in a stalemate. The winner then gets a chance to strike first, and the loser is pushed back or hurt. A push at level 3 can break a lock.

cards.name: Bryar pistol and charged shot
cards.summary: The starting pistol does 14 damage at 1800 units per second. Holding alt-fire charges a shot in 200 millisecond steps up to 5 and multiplies the damage by the step count, up to 70.
cards.behavior: Main fire sends one bolt with 14 damage and no spread for the player. Alt-fire holds the weapon in a charge state. On release the step count is the held time divided by 200 milliseconds, with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 5. The damage is the base damage times that count. Ammo use also scales with the count and is cut if the pool is short. The bolt can bounce up to 8 times, and sabers can deflect it. NPC fire adds spread that shrinks as their aim stat improves. These damage values are the built-in fallback table. The retail game may override them from a data file that this repository does not include. Fire interval values live in that file too, so they are unverified.

cards.name: E11 blaster rifle and enemy bolt tuning
cards.summary: The rifle bolt does 20 damage at 2300 units per second with 0.5 degree random spread. Alt-fire has the same damage and 1.5 degrees of spread. Enemy bolts are slower and weaker, scaled by difficulty.
cards.behavior: Main fire adds a uniform random offset of up to 0.5 degrees on pitch and yaw. Alt-fire uses up to 1.5. Stormtroopers use their aim stat. Their spread is 0.5 plus 0.25 per point that the current aim is below 6. When an NPC shoots, the bolt speed is cut to 50 percent on easy and medium and to 70 percent on hard so the player can dodge. NPC damage is 6 on easy, 12 on medium and 16 on hard. All bolts bounce up to 8 times and can be reflected by sabers. These are fallback table values and the shipped data file is not in this repository.

cards.name: Disruptor rifle zoom charge shot
cards.summary: Main fire is a hitscan shot for 14 damage out to 8192 units. When zoomed, the main button charges the alt shot in 150 millisecond steps up to 10. Damage is 12 per step plus 7 and the shot pierces more targets as it charges.
cards.behavior: Main fire traces a line of 8192 units and applies 14 damage to the first damageable hit. The player charges only while zoomed in, and then the main button acts as the charge input. On release the count is the held time minus 50 milliseconds, divided by 150, from 1 to 10. Damage is 12 times the count plus half of the main damage, so a full charge does 127. A count under 3 pierces 1 target. A count under 6 pierces 2. Higher counts pierce 3, which is the alt trace limit. Full charge marks the shot as a sniper kill. Jedi can dodge the trace. Other actors use fixed alt damage by difficulty of 15, 25 and 30. Force powers cannot be used while zoomed in.

cards.name: Bowcaster charged fan shot
cards.summary: Main fire charges in 200 millisecond steps and releases 1, 3 or 5 bolts in a 5 degree fan. Each bolt does 45 damage at about 1300 units per second. Alt-fire is one bouncing bolt.
cards.behavior: Holding main fire charges the weapon. On release the bolt count is the held time divided by 200 milliseconds, from 1 to 5. An even count is reduced by 1, so the result is 1, 3 or 5. Bolts spread sideways across a 5 degree step each, centered on the aim. Each bolt gets its own speed within 30 percent above or below the base. A short charge under 3 steps recovers fast, with the fire delay scaled to 35 percent. Ammo cost scales with the count. Alt-fire sends one bolt at the base speed that bounces up to 3 times. Bolts have no splash. The main bolt count and spread are live code. The fan is a distinct shotgun-like shape for this rifle.

constants.name: speed variation
constants.unit: fraction of base speed, each way

cards.name: Heavy repeater and flechette modes
cards.summary: The repeater fires 8 damage bolts at 1600 with 1.4 degree spread. Its alt shot is a 60 damage grenade at 1100 with a 128 unit blast. The flechette fires 6 shards at 3500 with 4 degree spread and an alt lob that explodes.
cards.behavior: Repeater main fire is a rapid stream of small bolts. Its alt-fire is a slow large shell that deals direct damage and an equal splash within a radius of 128 units. Bolts can bounce up to 8 times. The flechette main fire sends 6 pellets in one shot, each with a random offset of up to 4 degrees, each doing 15, and each bouncing once or twice. The flechette alt-fire lobs a shell at 950 plus up to 700 units per second that lives for 1500 plus up to 2000 milliseconds and explodes with 20 damage and 20 splash in a 128 unit radius. The flechette mine code and its constants are not used by the live fire path. Enemies fire the flechette at half speed. Both guns are blocked from deflection on high difficulty.

constants.name: flechette alt base speed
constants.unit: units per second, plus up to 700

cards.name: Rocket lock-on, thermal and mines
cards.summary: The rocket does 100 direct and 100 splash in 160 units at 900 speed. Alt-fire halves speed and homes after a 1200 millisecond lock. The thermal throw scales with hold time. Tripwire and proximity mines do 150 and 90 splash.
cards.behavior: Rocket main fire flies straight at 900 units per second. Alt-fire flies at half speed and can lock on. The lock builds across 8 slices over 1200 milliseconds. A full lock always homes. A partial lock homes with a chance that grows with the slices, and any lock has a small random chance of success. The homing turn is limited, so rockets cannot reverse. The thermal throw speed is 900 times the hold time divided by 900 milliseconds, clamped from 15 percent to 100 percent, with 120 units per second of upward lift. The thermal explodes 4000 milliseconds after the throw for both modes. The constants for alt thermal speed and time in the header are not read by the throw code. Trip mines stick to surfaces with a 1000 millisecond arming delay. Main fire makes a tripwire. Alt-fire makes a proximity mine that sets off at 190 units from an enemy and blows itself after 40 seconds.

cards.name: Health, armor and difficulty scaling
cards.summary: Max health is 100. Armor takes all damage while it is above half of max health, then 40 percent of each hit. Enemy health rises by a quarter per difficulty step except Jedi. The player always starts with the pistol and the saber.
cards.behavior: Armor works in two bands. While the armor value is above half of the max health the armor absorbs the full hit, limited by what is left. Below that, the armor absorbs 40 percent, rounded up, and health takes the rest. Some damage types skip armor. Fall damage and grip damage are examples. A personal shield fills armor to 100. The AT-ST pilot has armor that takes everything. Enemy health with a set value rises by one quarter per difficulty step, so 100, 125 and 150 percent. Reborn, shadow troopers and Jedi are excluded. The old rule that scaled damage taken by the player is commented out and not live. The player spawns with the pistol equipped and both pistol and saber in the inventory, unless the spawn point asks for a stun baton instead of the saber. All ammo types start full. Spawn grants a 100 millisecond knockback state, so full run speed returns slowly.

constants.name: enemy health step divisor
constants.unit: divisor, one quarter per difficulty step

cards.name: Stormtrooper detection of the player
cards.summary: A trooper wakes at once if the player is within 40 units, or 100 with a lit saber. Beyond that a rating of distance, view angle, light, speed and turning must pass 0.6. Between 0.45 and 0.6 the trooper turns to look first.
cards.behavior: The check runs only if no enemy is set. A target closer than 40 units is noticed at once. With the saber lit and in hand it is 100 units. The target must be within 1024 units, or the actor view range if larger, and inside the view cone. A distance below 7.5 percent of the view range also counts as noticed. The rating adds a distance part scaled 0.35, a view angle part scaled 0.4 and a light part scaled 0.25, and then adds bonuses for fast movement and head turning of up to 0.25 each. Water and fog subtract 10 to 35 percent. A crouching target is rated 10 percent lower. A dark target with a light level under 0.1 is never seen. The rating above 0.6 sets the enemy and an attack delay of 0.5 to 2.5 seconds. A rating above 0.45 times 0.75 makes the trooper look toward the target for 4.5 to 8.5 seconds and then investigate.
capabilities: rated sight check with distance, view, light and motion
closer wake range for a lit saber

cards.name: Trooper aim error and covering fire
cards.summary: Aim improves and degrades in steps on a timer of 500 plus 100 per missing skill level, with 0 to 1000 milliseconds added. Troopers that lose sight fire at the last seen spot, with a 1 in 11 chance per check.
cards.behavior: Each trooper has a current aim that moves toward a maximum aim stat. It can fall as low as -30. Aim only changes when a debounce timer ends. The debounce is 500 plus 100 times the missing difficulty steps, plus a random 0 to 1000 milliseconds. Spread then follows from the current aim. A trooper with no sight line may still fire at the last seen spot for up to 10 seconds, but only when a squad mate is moving, retreating or scouting, and only with a 1 in 11 chance. The shot is skipped if it would land closer than 128 units to the shooter, or 256 for explosives. After 5 seconds without sight it is skipped if it would land more than 256 units, or 512 for explosives, from where the target was last seen. Rocket users hold fire inside 128 units. On hard, troopers turn 1.5 times faster. On easy they turn 0.75 times as fast.

constants.name: covering fire chance roll
constants.unit: random roll 0 to 10, fire on zero

capabilities: aim stat that drifts over time
covering fire on the last seen position

cards.name: Reborn stance by rank and aggression limits
cards.summary: Grunts and fencers always use fast swings. Acrobats and force users always use medium. Bosses start strong. Others pick any stance and may reroll every 3 to 10 seconds. Aggression stays in 3 to 10 for enemies.
cards.behavior: Each enemy duelist is given a stance by rank when the saber is set up. The two weakest ranks use fast. The next two use medium. The boss rank starts strong. Shadow troopers pick a random stance. The dark lord and the female boss have their own special stance numbers. When idle, an unconstrained duelist has a 1 in 11 chance per check to pick a random stance, with a delay of 3 to 10 seconds before the next change. The delay is 1 to 5 seconds while fighting. Aggression is a number that sets how hard the duelist presses. Enemies are kept between 3 and 10. Allies are kept between 1 and 7. The dark lord uses 5 to 20. When aggression falls below 4 with no enemy, the saber is turned off.

cards.name: Reborn parry reaction time by difficulty
cards.summary: The base delay before a duelist can parry again is 200, 100 or 50 milliseconds on easy, medium and hard. Rank multiplies it. On hard the delay is a random 0 to 150. Lock winners press the attack at a rank-based chance.
cards.behavior: After a block the duelist waits a time before the next block. The base time follows the difficulty. Tavion halves it. Fencers and above use the base value, and one time in three they use half. Grunts multiply the base by 1 to 3. Acrobats multiply parries by 1 to 2. Force users multiply by 1 to 2. Ducking adds 100, jumping adds 50, and other evasion adds 100. On hard the base rule is replaced by a random 0 to 150 for all but Tavion, who has none. With the saber in flight the delay is 50 to 150. After winning a lock, the duelist has a chance to attack first. The chance is 20 out of 31 for the two bosses and 10 out of 31 for the dark apprentice. Fencers get 5 and others use their rank value. Duelists only swing in melee when closer than 64 units.

cards.name: Third-person camera for the saber
cards.summary: Drawing the saber switches the view to third person. Holstering to a gun switches back to first person. The camera sits 80 units behind a point 16 units above the eye and follows with damped motion.
cards.behavior: Two switches default to on. Drawing the saber turns third person on. Switching to any gun turns it off. Zooming always forces first person. Death and walker piloting force third person. The camera target is the view height plus a vertical offset of 16. The camera sits 80 units back along the view line. The follow uses a damping factor of 0.3 that grows with the square of pitch so that looking up or down is stiffer. The target uses 0.5. The factor is used as an exponent on the remaining distance, so the speed is frame-rate independent, with a time unit of 50 milliseconds. A cube with half extent 4 sweeps from the target to the camera so the camera never enters walls. Crouching nudges the focus up by 6. The field of view is 80 degrees.

constants.name: camera damping
constants.unit: fraction of remaining distance per damp interval

constants.name: target damping
constants.unit: fraction of remaining distance per damp interval
